sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The worker enteric valve architecture (EVA) is of the finitimus type; the workers are large within the genus and the enteric valve is also large, the odd primary cushion elongation index especially high (WVPOdd-Elg = 8.60–11.6). The soldier is medium-sized within the genus, its mandibles almost straight, the left mandible apical curvature index low (SMlc/SMlL = 0.05–0.07), as in I. minitabundus and I. ugandensis, but the latter two have the fungifaber type of EVA. The only known alate is medium-sized, with medium-sized compound eyes set far from the head margin and near the ocelli. The species is also defined by ecology and distribution: it is known only from Angolan woodlands.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Very similar to the alate of I. finitimus. Head capsule well sclerotized and very dark (C7); frontal gland pore paler than the head capsule; postclypeus C5, paler than the head capsule; antennae C5. Pronotum C7, concolorous with the head capsule; meso- and metanotum C6; legs C4–C5, the tibiae one shade darker than the femora; wings transparent with a brown to grey tinge (Cf3), the costa darker; abdominal tergites C6; sternites distinctly paler in the middle (C3), darker at the sides (C5), the posterior sternites (C5) darker than the anterior ones. Head capsule with conspicuous setae scattered among the dense felt of short fine hairs; labrum and postclypeus with conspicuous setae mixed with short hairs; antennae with conspicuous setae and more numerous small hairs, most segments with a tuft of very fine curved hairs at the tip, especially distally (visible above 50×). Pronotum setae mainly on the margins, shorter in the middle; meso- and metanotum without visible setae, even at 100×. Legs hairy, the fore coxa with 6 stronger setae, the trochanter with 4–5; fore, mid and hind tibiae with 3, 2 and 2 apical spurs and 0, 2 and 0 subapical spurs respectively, the tibiae with 20–35 spines. Abdominal tergites with setae of mixed sizes; sternites with long setae erect or slightly inclined forward, together with many long and small setae directed posteriorly. Compound eyes short-oval; ocelli short-oval, separated from the compound eye by about 0.7–0.8 times the small ocellar diameter; frontal gland pore generally a small circular or elongate mark. Antennae 16-segmented (the only known alate). Labrum domed. Left mandible apical tooth always more prominent than the first marginal tooth; 3 marginal teeth, the second expressed only as an undulation of the tooth margin between the first and third; only the apical tooth sharp in unworn specimens; the proximal premolar hidden or partly hidden by the molar prominence in dorsal view; the dorsal surface of the molar with a rounded prominence ending posteriorly in a small sharp process. Right mandible apical tooth always more prominent than the first marginal tooth; 2 marginal teeth, the first sharp-tipped when fresh, the second smaller and blunt even when fresh; the molar with a rounded labial process ventrally and heel-shaped posteriorly. Pronotum distinctly wider than long, narrower than the head width (including compound eyes), flat to very weakly saddle-shaped, the anterior lobe short and very slightly raised; the lip-like projection on the ventral surface of the fore coxa weak, the ridge indistinct. Wings: R1 completely fused with the margin and sclerotized; Rs single and sclerotized; M and Cu unsclerotized or weakly sclerotized, with 3 and 9 branches respectively. Measurements (the only known alate): compound eye major diameter 0.42 mm, head width including compound eyes 1.60 mm, distance from the apical tooth to the first marginal tooth 0.21 mm, ocellus major diameter 0.18 mm, postclypeus width 0.82 mm, pronotum width 1.34 mm, hind tibia length 1.93 mm, fore wing length to the suture 15.9 mm.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head capsule C4–C5, the frons C5–C6; gulamentum slightly darker than the head; antennae and labrum concolorous with the head capsule; mandibles dark (C7–C8), the base abruptly two shades paler and concolorous with the frons; thorax, tergites and legs slightly paler than the head capsule (C3–C4); abdomen grey to red-brown from the gut contents, the tergites very rarely with a pale yellow tinge. Head capsule with a few scattered setae; a dense tuft of hairs surrounds and covers the frontal gland pore; antennae with conspicuous setae and more numerous small hairs, the apical segment with a tuft of fine curved hairs at its tip (visible above 50×); the labrum with several large setae on each lobe; pronotum and mesonotum with setae mainly on the margins. Fore coxa with 1–3 spines on the ridge and 0–1 ventrally; trochanter with 3–6 long spines in a row; fore, mid and hind tibiae with 3, 2 and 2 apical spurs and 0, 2 and 0 subapical spurs respectively, each tibia with a row of 9–15 spines. Abdominal tergites with the large setae mainly on the posterior margin; sternites with long setae erect or slightly inclined forward and often pigmented, together with smaller setae directed posteriorly. Soldier medium-sized within the genus. Head capsule distinctly sclerotized, distinctly longer than wide; in dorsal view the sides usually nearly parallel, slightly narrowing in the posterior third, distinctly converging from the antennal sockets towards the mandible bases, the posterior margin regularly convex; the upper margin concave in lateral view; the frons with a distinct frontal swelling covering the frontal gland pore. Gulamentum narrowing in the posterior half in ventral view, the anterior half widening at sharp angles and with ear-like projections. Antennae 15-segmented. Labrum deeply forked, wider than long, the sides harp-shaped; the lobes angular or truncate, their tips fine, white or semitransparent; the anterior margin concave. Mandibles sabre-like, almost straight basally and slightly curved distally; the left mandible apical curvature index very low (SMlc/SMlL < 0.075); the inner margin smooth, each mandible with 1 distinct but very small marginal tooth near the molar area; mandibles distinctly shorter than the head; the surface of both smooth and shining. Pronotum saddle-shaped, distinctly narrower than the head, the anterior margin sometimes with a shallow notch, the posterior margin entire; the fore coxa with a lip-like projection ventrally forming a sharp ridge. Enteric valve inserted on the left side, best seen in ventral view, in the posterior half of the abdomen. Primary cushions (PC) arranged with trigonal symmetry, the odd cushion 19% longer than the even ones, the crest weak; secondary cushions (SC) broad upstream, distinctly narrowing downstream, the spines evenly distributed. Caecum small, best seen in ventral view, near the middle of the abdomen, lobed (3 lobules). Measurements: head dorsal concavity sagitta 0.04–0.09 mm, head length 3.04–3.41 mm, head width 2.06–2.34 mm, left mandible ventral length 2.33–2.63 mm, left mandible minor curvature 0.13–0.19 mm, hind tibia length 1.74–1.89 mm.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head capsule pale (C1–C3); proximal antennal segments pale (C2), the apical segment two shades darker (C4); thorax, tergites and legs pale (C1–C3); abdomen grey to red-brown from the gut contents. Head capsule and postclypeus with a few scattered erect setae; labrum with a few scattered stout setae; antennae with conspicuous setae and more numerous small hairs, the apical segment with a tuft of very fine curved hairs at its tip (visible above 50×); thoracic tergites with scattered setae. Fore coxa ridged, with 1 fine seta, 2–4 spines on the ridge and 0–2 ventrally; fore trochanter with 7–9 spines; fore, mid and hind tibiae with 3, 2 and 2 apical spurs and 0, 2 and 0 subapical spurs respectively, and with a row of 8–16 spines. Abdominal tergites with scattered setae; sternites with long setae erect or slightly inclined forward and often pigmented, together with smaller setae directed posteriorly. Workers medium-sized to large within the genus. Head capsule weakly sclerotized (except the mandibles). Antennae 14–14.5 segmented. Labrum domed. Left mandible with a well-developed apical tooth (distance from the apical tooth to the first marginal tooth WMlAmD > 0.19 mm), sharp-tipped when fresh; 3 marginal teeth, the first well developed but blunt even when fresh, the second weak (expressed only as an undulating tooth margin), the third with a blunt tip; the premolar more easily seen than in most species of the genus; the dorsal surface of the molar with a rounded prominence ending posteriorly in a small sharp process. Right mandible with a well-developed apical tooth, sharp when fresh; 2 marginal teeth, the first well developed and sharp when fresh, the second smaller and blunt even when fresh; the molar with a rounded labial process ventrally and heel-shaped posteriorly. Pronotum saddle-shaped, 63%–70% of the head width; the fore coxa with a lip-like projection ventrally forming a sharp ridge. Enteric valve inserted on the left, best seen in ventral view, in the posterior half of the abdomen. Primary cushions arranged in the finitimus type with trigonal symmetry: the downstream part of the odd cushion is broad, its bulbous inflation bearing very dense shorter setae; supporting setae generally numerous, 25–33 on each side of the odd cushion; the worker enteric valve very large (mean length WVP-AvL > 0.72 mm), the odd primary cushion elongation index very high; secondary cushions broad upstream, distinctly narrowing downstream, the spines evenly distributed. Caecum small, visible in ventral view, near the middle of the abdomen, with short lobes (3 lobules). Measurements: maximum head width 1.25–1.34 mm, distance from the apical tooth to the first marginal tooth 0.20–0.21 mm, left mandible functional length 0.59–0.65 mm, hind tibia length 1.35–1.41 mm, mean length of primary cushions 1–6 0.73–0.75 mm, mean width 0.07–0.09 mm, mean length of secondary cushions 0.59–0.64 mm, mean width 0.32–0.41 mm, odd primary cushion elongation index WVPOdd-Elg = 8.60–11.6.

note: Adapted from the genus revision in Josens et al. (2025), original in English; measurements of the alate and soldier from Table 13 of the original (a single alate only); distribution, hosts, DNA and figure numbers are not translated.
